title: Perimeter and Area on the Coordinate Plane
short: Use the distance formula to find perimeters and areas.

blocks.html: When a figure's vertices are given as coordinates, the distance formula from Distance and Midpoint Formulas finds every side, so you can find its perimeter. For area, a rectangle drawn around the figure turns a slanted shape into pieces you already know.

Sides along grid lines are easy: count. Slanted sides come from the Pythagorean theorem, so they are often square roots. Only like radicals combine: $\sqrt{8} + \sqrt{2} = 2\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{2} = 3\sqrt{2}$, but $\sqrt{5} + \sqrt{13}$ stays as it is. For area, the box method works because the box is a rectangle and the leftover corner pieces are right triangles (and rectangles) whose legs lie along the grid.

blocks.name: geoboard
blocks.cap: Drag the vertices. The readout gives each side length, the perimeter and the area.

blocks.html: Perimeter: add the side lengths from the distance formula, simplifying radicals and combining like ones. Area: enclose the figure in a grid-aligned rectangle and subtract the right triangles and rectangles in the corners.

blocks.title: A perimeter with radicals
blocks.q: Find the perimeter of the triangle with $A(1, 1)$, $B(7, 1)$ and $C(3, 5)$.

blocks.title: The box method
blocks.q: Find the area of the triangle with $A(1, 1)$, $B(7, 2)$ and $C(3, 6)$.
steps: The box from $x = 1$ to $7$ and $y = 1$ to $6$ is $6 \times 5 = 30$.

blocks.title: A right triangle on the grid
blocks.q: Find the area and perimeter of the triangle with $P(-2, -1)$, $Q(4, -1)$ and $R(-2, 7)$.
steps: $\overline{PQ}$ is horizontal (length 6) and $\overline{PR}$ is vertical (length 8): a right angle at $P$.

blocks.html: Adding unlike radicals, like $\sqrt{32} + \sqrt{20} = \sqrt{52}$. Square roots do not add that way: $\sqrt{32} + \sqrt{20} \approx 5.66 + 4.47 = 10.13$, but $\sqrt{52} \approx 7.21$. Simplify each radical, then combine only the ones with the same number under the root.
